>
> How can I do this with ggplot2?
> a) per variable, save a png with a geom_line of value x year?

Use variable for faceting. See http://docs.ggplot2.org/current/facet_wrap.html

You'll probably want free y-scales due to the extreme differences in
value between levels of variable, something like
... + facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free_y")
You don't need free x-scales since they are the same for each level of variable.

>
> b) save a unique pdf with plots (perhaps 8 per page) for all variables
> using geom_line of values x year?

Use variable as an aesthetic (e.g., color or linetype). See
http://docs.ggplot2.org/current/geom_line.html

and for the legend colors, perhaps
http://docs.ggplot2.org/current/scale_brewer.html

>
> c) produce one plot of two selected variables, say trunoff and srunoff,
> with two geom_lines of values x year?

subdata <- subset(origdata, variable %in% c("srunoff", "trunoff"))
subdata$variable <- droplevels(subdata$variable)

and use subdata in the ggplot() call with the color/linetype aesthetic.

Dennis

> How can I do this with ggplot2?
>   a) per variable, save a png with a geom_line of value x year?

Use variable for faceting. See http://docs.ggplot2.org/current/facet_wrap.html

You'll probably want free y-scales due to the extreme differences in
value between levels of variable, something like
  ... + facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free_y")
You don't need free x-scales since they are the same for each level of variable.

>
>   b) save a unique pdf with plots (perhaps 8 per page) for all variables
> using geom_line of values x year?

Use variable as an aesthetic (e.g., color or linetype). See
http://docs.ggplot2.org/current/geom_line.html

and for the legend colors, perhaps
http://docs.ggplot2.org/current/scale_brewer.html

>
>   c) produce one plot of two selected variables, say trunoff and srunoff,
> with two geom_lines of values x year?

subdata <- subset(origdata, variable %in% c("srunoff", "trunoff"))
subdata$variable <- droplevels(subdata$variable)

and use subdata in the ggplot() call with the color/linetype aesthetic.
